sentences.text: The prosecution has based its case on the fact that Manoj PW-3 has developed intimacy with the sister of his friend.
On 22.06.2019, they both planned to left the home and live together.

In execution of this plan, the complainant Manoj PW-3 rented a Tevera Vehicle reached at Bercha at 01:00AM in the night, took the sister of his friend and stayed at the accommodation of one another friend.
Another day, both went to village Kankariaya, Ujjain.

On 26.06.2009, when Manoj PW-3 and the girl went to take water from the house of one Pramod Upadhayay then, at that time, the appellants reached there,
took Manoj PW-3 and the girl, assaulted and caused injuries to Manoj PW-3 and extended threat to kill him.

4. On the complaint, a case under Section 366, 376, 343, 506 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:37692 3 CRA-959-2010 of IPC was registered at Police Station Berchha, District Shajapur at Crime No.89/2009 against Manoj PW-3 and Crime No.490/2009 was also registered against the appellants at Police Station Neelganga, Ujjain.
5. The appellants were prosecuted and they abjured the guilt.

6. To bring home the guilt, the prosecution has examined as many as 11 witnesses including the complainant Manoj PW-3, Abdul Ishak PW-1, ASI Shejad Beg PW-2, Sunil Upadhayay PW-4, Dr.
Jairam Chouhan PW-5, Subhash Upadhayay PW-6, Dr. N.K. Gupta PW-7, Arun PW-8, Ahok Patidar PW-9, ASI SL Sharma, PW-10 and TM Chouhan PW-11.
7. Appreciating the evidence, the learned trial Court has convicted and sentenced the appellants as mentioned in para no.1, above of the judgment.
8. Challenging the conviction and the sentence, this criminal appeal has been preferred.
9. During the pendency of this appeal, the complainant Manoj PW-3 and the appellants have entered into compromise.
The compromise was verified by the Principal Registrar of this Court in both the criminal appeals on 12.01.2018.

10. On the basis of compromise entered between the parties, the appellants are acquitted from the offence under section 147 and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37692 4 CRA-959-2010 506 of IPC.
11.

Considering the statements of Manoj PW-3, ASI Shejad Beg PW-2, Sunil Upadhayay PW-4,
Subhash Upadhayay PW-6, Dr. N.K. Gupta PW-7, Arun PW-8, ASI SL Sharma, PW-10 and TM Chouhan PW-11, conviction of the appellants under Section 364 and 365 of IPC does not required for interference.
Hence, the conviction of the appellants under section 364 and 365 of IPC stands affirmed.

2 12.
So far as the sentence of the appellants is concerned, each of the appellants have already undergone approximately 50-55 days.

Considering the genesis of the incident and the factum of compromise between the parties, no purpose would be served if the appellants are sent in jail again after a lapse of approximately 17 years of the incident.
Hence, the appeals are partly allowed and the sentence of the appellants is modified to the extant that the sentence of the appellants is reduced to the period already undergone.
13. A copy of this judgment be sent to the learned trial Court concerned for information.
